title: Letter and Verdict Again
premise: When a drowned man washes up in Hollow Creek wearing clothes stolen from coroner Quentin Eastwick's own closet, the investigation drags her into the decade-old death of Ada Voss — a case closed by a signed confession that Quentin herself notarized. As she reopens old wounds, she discovers the confession was coerced by the town's beloved retired judge, who has been silencing witnesses ever since. The new victim was Ada's brother, killed before he could recant testimony. In the end, Quentin must choose between protecting the town's fragile peace and delivering the truth: she testifies against the judge at trial, closing both cases with a verdict that costs her every friend she has but frees an innocent man.
about_author: Cyrus Quintana is a former rural court clerk whose years of transcribing small-town verdicts left him fascinated by what never made it into the record. He writes mysteries from a farmhouse in upstate New York, where he claims to know his own county's graves by name.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A body surfaces in Hollow Creek dressed in Quentin's own missing suit, and Sheriff Dane treats her as witness, suspect, and coroner all at once. She identifies the victim as Milo Voss, brother of a girl whose death Quentin helped close ten years ago. The beat is unease: the case has followed her home.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Walking the cemetery to clear her head, she recalls notarizing Milo's sister Ada's confession a decade ago and notices fresh flowers on Ada's grave — placed by someone who shouldn't care anymore. Her assistant Ruth urges her to let it lie. The beat is dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Confession File
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with a flashback interlude in Ada's voice. Quentin pulls the sealed file and finds pages out of order and a signature dated before the interrogation began. When she asks the retired Judge Harlan Bell about it over coffee, his warmth turns glacial. The beat is the first crack in the town's official memory.

chapters.title: Witness for the Closet
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth admits she saw someone leaving Quentin's house the night the suit vanished — and recognizes the silhouette as Deputy Colm Reyes, the judge's protégé. She sits on the information, torn between loyalty to the office and to Quentin. The beat is complicity: silence as a kind of theft.

chapters.title: What Ada Said
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin tracks down Ada's old schoolteacher, who reveals Ada recanted her confession days before dying in a 'single-car accident.' The teacher hands over an unsent letter naming Harlan Bell. That night, Quentin's garage is ransacked and the letter stolen. The beat is escalation — the past fighting back.

chapters.title: The Judge's House
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin confronts Bell at home; he offers her the coroner's seat for life if she closes Milo's case as an accident. She finds Milo's watch on Bell's mantel, taken from the body before she ever logged it. The beat is temptation met with quiet menace — justice offered a price.

chapters.title: Colm Breaks
chapters.summary: Colm's POV. Cornered by Quentin with evidence of the break-in, Colm confesses he moved the body on Bell's orders and stole the suit to frame her, believing he was protecting the town from scandal. He agrees to testify, then vanishes before dawn. The beat is betrayal and the collapse of the cover-up's spine.

chapters.title: Hollow Creek Turns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs — Dane, Ruth, townsfolk voices. Bell spins the story publicly: Quentin is a grieving woman unhinged by guilt. Quentin loses her office pending review, and old friends cross the street to avoid her. The beat is isolation at the bottom of the arc — truth making her a stranger.

chapters.title: The Verdict Before the Trial
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Colm resurfaces at the courthouse with Bell's ledger of hush payments; Dane, choosing law over loyalty, arrests Bell for Milo's murder and the obstruction in Ada's death. Bell, arraigned, stares at Quentin across the courtroom. The beat is catharsis — the machinery of justice finally turning toward her.

chapters.title: Letter and Verdict Again
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, epilogue months later. On the stand, Quentin delivers the testimony that convicts Bell; Ada's unsent letter, recovered from Bell's safe, is read aloud. Milo's case closes as murder, Ada's as one reopened too late. Quentin buries the suit and plants flowers on two graves. The beat is costly peace — truth kept, loyalty spent.
